scope: CPU graph and registered split analysis only; no training results, checkpoints or predictions read

definitions.mean_exposures_per_record: steps * batch_size / (atomic_count + sampled_composite_count); uniform shuffled epochs, actual records differ by at most one presentation
definitions.atomic_training_examples_proportional_ex: mean_exposures_per_record * atomic_count; exact partial-epoch atomic count is not simulated
definitions.test_denominator: entire reserved ID test pool, not the fixed 1024-example probe
definitions.same_position_atomic_coverage: Each constituent (head, relation, tail) occurred at that same hop in at least one training composition; this is data exposure, not learned correctness
definitions.relation_sequence_coverage: Ordered relation tuple alone appeared in training, regardless of starting entity
definitions.subpath_coverage: Actual intermediate starting entity plus ordered relation subsequence appeared at the same starting hop in a training composition; these subpaths are not separately supervised
definitions.invariance: Exact equality of graph, atomic split, full test pool and test probe across phi is asserted
definitions.training_sets: Uniform samples without replacement at each phi; samples need not be nested

worlds.array_hash_encoding: little-endian int64 shape followed by array bytes
little-endian int64 shape followed by array bytes

recommendation.retain: k3-d4 and k4-d6 architectures, width, learning rate, initialization, full test pool, probe, 128000 updates and batch256
recommendation.basis: phi6 already gives about 98% test coverage of atomic facts at their hop positions and complete adjacent-relation-pair coverage; phi24 raises same-position two-hop-subpath coverage to about 95-97% while preserving more per-record exposure than phi48
recommendation.prerequisite: Check atomic and training-composition learning in development; data coverage alone does not explain an optimization failure
recommendation.interpretation: One development data-amount calibration; no guarantee of success, no depth-law claim, and no trained-sample or model-result selection in this analysis
